name: Isomorphic_Problem_Class_Baiting
description: I replaced the contrived checksum narrative with a pristine, mathematically unambiguous boolean logic constraint: `(x_u OR x_v) AND (NOT x_u OR NOT x_v)`. This perfectly preserves the undirected `x_u != x_v` semantics and eliminates the ambiguity flagged by the expert. However, by framing it as boolean clauses, it strongly baits surface-pattern-matching models into treating the problem as general 2-SAT. Standard 2-SAT algorithms fail to produce the lexicographically smallest assignment required by the tie-breaker, and greedy 2-SAT approaches will Time Out (O(N^2)). Only models that genuinely reason that these specific clauses reduce to a simple bipartite graph will use the required O(N+M) BFS approach to succeed.
